clue.text: Very backward family with name right round Croatian port

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the word for family from its last letter to its first

blocks.note: to dub someone is to give them a name
R is the standard abbreviation for right
a round shape is the letter O
V is the abbreviation for very
your kin are your family

explanation.surface: Someone describes a backward family arriving with a name in tow at a port on the Adriatic.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are written in a different order from the clue: DUB, R and O come first, then V and NIK.
explanation.definitionFit: The walled city on the Adriatic coast is a major harbour and tourist destination in southern Croatia.

clue.text: Journalist supporting political party, taken for a ride

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath, so this piece comes second

blocks.note: the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A reporter backing a party ends up being conned.
explanation.definitionFit: Being taken for a ride is an idiom for being cheated or deceived by someone.

clue.text: Pub profit dishonourable blokes finally spent in sales area

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
gain is profit
base means morally low
blokes are men
the closing letter of spent

explanation.surface: Pub profits are squandered by shady men shopping in a sale.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest floor of a department store, where cut-price goods are sold, is a discount shopping zone.

clue.text: Herb old miners planted outside Baltic port

indicators.note: planted outside means set beside rather than within, so the miners follow the port

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
Riga is the capital and port of Latvia
the NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers

explanation.surface: Some veteran miners have planted a herb outside a Baltic port.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the botanical genus of marjoram and oregano, aromatic plants used in cooking.

clue.text: Source of information recalled uplands and city

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the pieces are read backwards

blocks.note: moors are high open uplands
the Great Wen is an old nickname for London, so a wen is a big city

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a source talking about the hills and the town.
explanation.definitionFit: The office where journalists gather and edit stories supplies reports to the public as a hub of news.

clue.text: King longing to restrict son’s trashy material

indicators.note: restricting something hems it in, so one letter goes inside the word

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
an itch is a longing or craving
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A king's craving is curbed, keeping his son from rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes inside ITCH, after K; the 's on son's is part of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes art or objects in poor taste, garish and sentimental, so it is tacky stuff.

clue.text: Woman keeping record in regimental HQ

indicators.note: a woman keeping something holds it inside her, so one word goes within another

blocks.note: Dot is a woman's name, short for Dorothy
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A woman keeps some record or file at the headquarters of a regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment's headquarters, where recruits are trained and stores held, is traditionally called its base or barracks depot.

clue.text: Young chap upset girl over scene of assassination

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top
over means turned over, so the name is read backwards

blocks.note: a lad is a young chap
Sal is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young man upsets a girl at the scene of a killing.
explanation.definitionFit: President John F Kennedy was shot dead in this Texas city in November 1963.

clue.text: Bird of prey foreign cleaner disturbed after parking

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird of prey upsets a cleaner from abroad who has just parked.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fast-diving raptor, famed as the quickest animal on Earth, that hunts other birds.

clue.text: Extremely tender, ancient man, one playing Lear perhaps

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

blocks.note: the outside letters of tender
aged means very old
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: A very gentle old man is cast as King Lear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Lear is a tragic role in Shakespeare, so an actor taking it is a performer of tragedy.

clue.text: Turning up readily at first, struggle with range

indicators.note: turning the following little word around means reading it backwards
at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned
the opening letter of readily
to vie is to struggle or compete
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: Someone readily turns up to struggle across a whole range of tasks.
explanation.walkthrough: UP turned gives PU; 'with' does double duty, as W rather than a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Purview means the scope or extent of someone's authority or concern, the field it covers.

clue.text: Winged sandals identified in short story and song

indicators.note: a short version of the word lacks its final letter

blocks.note: a tale is a story
an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: Mythical winged sandals turn up in a short story and a song.
explanation.walkthrough: TALE loses its last letter to give TAL.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical myth these were the winged shoes worn on the ankles of Hermes, messenger of the gods.

clue.text: Wee drink leading to a humiliating scene?

blocks.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits, a wee drink in Scots
taken as written

explanation.surface: One small drink leads to an embarrassing public scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a humiliating scene is only one kind of this word, an emotional fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a drama means creating a fuss or an embarrassing emotional display in front of others.

clue.text: Excitedly greet clan figure

indicators.note: doing something excitedly means in a jumbled, agitated way, so the letters are stirred up

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone excitedly greets a clan figure, like a chieftain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clan figure' reads as a person, but figure alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-sided plane shape with right angles is a geometric figure in the mathematical sense.

clue.text: Entertainer primarily concentrating on person in box

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so take only the opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of concentrating
taken as written
a juror sits in the jury box in court

explanation.surface: An entertainer focuses on a person shut in a box, as in a magic trick.
explanation.walkthrough: The box looks like a magician's cabinet, but it is the jury box.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician who performs tricks and illusions on stage is an entertainer by profession.

clue.text: Eg Spice Girl engaged by male fraudsters on time

indicators.note: something engaged by others is held within them, so one word goes inside another

blocks.note: con men are male swindlers
Di is a girl's name
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A Spice Girl is hired by male swindlers who are on the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Spice Girl looks like the pop group, but Spice is the definition and Girl gives the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Spices, sauces and relishes added to flavour food are seasonings, and a spice is one example.

clue.text: Female judge visiting islands in Pacific state

indicators.note: visiting a place means going inside it, so these letters sit within others

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for island, doubled for the plural
F is the abbreviation for female
J is the abbreviation for judge

explanation.surface: A female judge visits some islands in a Pacific nation.
explanation.walkthrough: F and J together go inside the pair of Is.
explanation.definitionFit: The archipelago nation in Melanesia, made up of over three hundred islands, is a sovereign country in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Dogsbody’s deed interrupting turning up of corporation

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so one word goes inside another
in a down clue, turning up means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned
an act is a deed
a corporation is jocular old slang for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: An assistant's act gets in the way of a company's reversal of fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation as a word for a pot belly is dated British humour, and the clue's company sense is the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A general servant or assistant who does every kind of job is a dogsbody, one who does all the menial work.

clue.text: Noisy bird with crest finally replaced by quiet dog

indicators.note: replaced by means one letter is swapped out for another
finally picks the last letter of the word before it as the one to be swapped

blocks.note: the cockatoo is a loud crested parrot
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A noisy crested bird is finally swapped for a quiet dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of crest is T; swap the T in COCKATOO for P.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross between a cocker spaniel and a poodle is a popular designer breed of pet.

clue.text: Well-groomed old farm animals

blocks.note: first meaning: tidy and smart in appearance
second meaning: an archaic word for cattle

explanation.surface: Some old farm animals have been nicely groomed for a show.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means tidy and orderly, while the old noun meant oxen or cattle, as in neatherd.

clue.text: Early seventeenth century woman astride a sturdy horse

indicators.note: someone astride a horse has a leg each side of it, so her name wraps around

blocks.note: Jean is a woman's name
taken as written
a cob is a short-legged, sturdy horse

explanation.surface: A woman of the early 1600s rides astride a strong horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is fair because the adjective comes from Jacobus, Latin for James, whose reign began in 1603.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the reign of James I of England, from 1603 to 1625, and its architecture and drama.

clue.text: Mastermind in part of family touring India

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so the word goes round a letter

blocks.note: in biology a genus is a subdivision of a family
India is I in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The brains of a family gang is touring India.
explanation.definitionFit: A brilliant person of exceptional intellect, the brains behind a scheme, is a mastermind.

clue.text: Ragamuffin, rather a scallywag at heart

indicators.note: at heart means deep inside, so the letters sit within the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A street urchin is, deep down, rather a scamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischievous child or rogue is a scamp, a scruffy young troublemaker.

clue.text: Unrefined modern worker taking in the Spanish, say

indicators.note: taking in means accepting something inside, so the following pieces go within

blocks.note: in means fashionable, of the moment
el is the Spanish for the
eg, for example, is what 'say' means
the worker ant is a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A modern labourer picks up some Spanish, perhaps the word for the.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' is not a homophone signal here; it stands for 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking grace, polish and style, something unrefined is clumsy or crude rather than graceful.

clue.text: Dangerous reptile artist found in equipment

indicators.note: something found in a bag is inside it, so one word sits within another

blocks.note: kit is equipment
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A dangerous snake is discovered lurking in a painter's gear.
explanation.definitionFit: This highly venomous snake of South and South-East Asia is among the deadliest serpents.

clue.text: Roofing contractor, say left in middle of row

indicators.note: in middle of means placed inside, so a letter goes within the word

blocks.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A roofer has left in the middle of an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, but it is a row of seats; 'say' shows the roofer is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lays tiles is a tradesperson, and one who tiles roofs is an example of a roofer.

clue.text: Mournful English member getting first clue

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a leg is a limb, a member of the body
the first clue in the grid is 1 across, written 1AC with I for one

explanation.surface: A gloomy English club member is handed the opening hint.
explanation.walkthrough: The self-reference is to this puzzle's own grid, where the first clue is 1 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes the tone of an elegy, a lament for the dead, so it means sorrowful.

clue.text: Current head I cite briefly

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: the top is the head of something
taken as written
to call or cite a witness

explanation.surface: A head teacher says 'I cite briefly' when quoting something recent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something topical deals with present-day matters of interest, so it is up to date.

clue.text: Upper-class scholar primarily associated with bird book

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: the tit is a small songbird
U means upper-class in British usage
the opening letter of scholar

explanation.surface: A posh scholar is closely linked with a book about birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird book' reads as one idea, but bird gives letters and book alone is the definition.

clue.text: Parodist’s poem Lorna revised

indicators.note: something revised has been reworked, so these letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A satirist has rewritten a poem called Lorna.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes satirical mockery of a person or work ridicules it, which is what a parodist does.
